uncertainty_notes: CC-02 fix (register-once-per-open-cycle via ref-based getter) is correctly implemented and well-tested. The test directly exercises the regression (5 re-renders with new arrow identities → still 1 listener), the LATEST-callback semantics, and the open=false↔true transitions. The getter indirection (line 29 comment) correctly avoids stale-closure trap. The lazy install/remove of the window listener (lines 41-51) is idempotent. No correctness or operator-impacting issues found.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for nested drawers (drawer B on top of drawer A) — the stated motivation for the whole module (#WR-01).
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: This is the load-bearing claim: Esc must dismiss ONLY the topmost drawer. A regression that fires Esc on all stacked drawers would collapse drilldowns in one keystroke, the exact bug this module exists to fix.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Open drawer A (push), open drawer B (push), dispatch Esc, assert only B's onClose was called and A's was NOT.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for cleanup order: if drawer A pops while drawer B is on top, the stack must correctly identify B as still topmost (uses lastIndexOf, so order-tolerant).
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Edge case: nested drawer close-from-middle. With current implementation it works, but no test pins behavior.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Push A, push B, pop A, dispatch Esc, assert B's callback fired.

exports_to: drawer components (DetailsDrawer, AdsDrawer, etc.) via useDrawerEsc
